facts.text: I've been having pain in my right foot.
It's in the sole of my right foot.

facts.item: foot pain: worse when the foot is raised
facts.text: It gets worse when I raise my foot above chest level during exercises.
I get cramps in my right calf when I use the incline on the treadmill.

facts.item: calf cramps with exercise: need to stop
facts.text: I have to take frequent breaks because of them.
The pain goes away completely after a few minutes of rest.
I don't have any other significant symptoms.
I've had type 2 diabetes for 8 years.
I smoke two packs of cigarettes a day and have done so for 34 years.
I started exercising regularly 2 months ago.

findings.name: straight-leg raise test
findings.result: Elicits pallor and tingling pain in the right foot.

findings.name: peripheral pulses
findings.result: Femoral pulses palpable; right pedal pulses absent.

findings.name: sensation
findings.result: No alterations besides tingling on straight-leg raise.

findings.name: back examination
findings.result: Inspection: no abnormalities. Palpation: no pain or tenderness. Range of motion: full, without discomfort.

findings.name: Doppler ultrasound of the right leg
findings.result: Evidence of significant femoropopliteal artery stenosis in the right leg.

quotes.f002: in the sole of his right foot
quotes.f004: worsens when he raises it above chest level during exercises
quotes.f006: right calf cramps with the use of the treadmill's incline feature
quotes.f008: The pain subsides completely after a few minutes of resting.
quotes.f011: Smokes two packs of cigarettes daily for 34 years.

f008: 'The pain subsides completely after a few minutes of resting' follows the calf-cramp sentence; it is not clear whether it refers to the calf cramps, the foot pain or both, so it is a standalone fact.

x003: The 'straight-leg raise' producing pallor of the foot is in effect a leg-elevation (Buerger) test; name kept as in the source with aliases.
x009: HbA1c 7.2% is labelled 'poor diabetes control' by the source; it is only slightly above a usual target of 7%.

leakage.reason: Doppler result states the gold diagnosis verbatim ('significant femoropopliteal artery stenosis'); it is the test's answer (pool flag: test_results).

source_issues: The Doppler result names the diagnosis verbatim (pool_flags.visible_gold_alias_partitions = test_results).
Only pulse and blood pressure are given as vital signs (no temperature or respiratory rate).
notes: The chief complaint ('Tingling pain in the sole of the right foot upon elevation') gives the opening: the foot pain with its location, tingling character and worsening on elevation as child facts.
The calf cramps with exercise and the foot pain are separate complaints; the 'need for frequent breaks' is a child of the calf cramps.
'No other significant symptoms reported' (p006) is read as a plain denial of other symptoms.

extras.objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with tingling pain in the sole of the right foot, especially upon elevation and during exercise, with a significant history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and smoking.
